Built: three-way closure reconciliation, exact host24, typedef-derived definitions, no erased virtual function pointers, and parser count regressions. Parser C/binary identity to main 48c05d09 still FAIL; current release best of five main 10.208 ms versus branch 10.854 ms.
Commits: census bf1a3823, host 14856bbf, front-3 ec485eab, main 28443efc, host24 9b6b451c, ABI enforcement 2b98fb26, all pushed on codex/closure-convention. Warning fa48dc2d is pushed on codex/arguments-length. This follow-up removes the obsolete count slot and pins the clean wrong-slot miscompile.
Commands and outputs: full native 156.042s, full IR 1.248s/lower 37.162s, class/nested/host24 Node gate 32.880s, non-null/union Node gate 16.829s, and touched-package go vet pass. Count-bearing regressions pass release, ASan/UBSan, JavaScript and leak checks.
Mutants: swapped definition/call, incompatible function-pointer cast, void-erased constructor and generated/runtime drop-count all fail compilation; clean wrong-slot 9-versus-1 fails only Node stdout comparison in release and sanitized builds. Prior excess-count, callback, filesystem and inheritance mutants remain caught.
Not covered: exact unpublished parser scratch 33bf53ac replay, parser byte identity, hardware instructions/cycles, blocked taste 21 full gate, and four external process/parallel runtime sites. A reconstruction verifies 64 of 77 front25 compiler-file postimages; 13 essential postimages remain unavailable, so no exact replay claim.

One convention

Plain code: adamic_code(self, arguments). Counted code: adamic_counted_code(self, arguments, argument_count).
Plain methods: adamic_method(self, arguments). Counted methods: adamic_counted_method(self, arguments, argument_count).
Each shape has exactly one typedef. No call uses a function-pointer cast. Typed union dispatch selects the shape of the actual closure or method.
Count observations include arguments.length, rest binding, and incompatible optional absence representations in the closed-world function-type candidate set. Compatible omitted slots are padded by the caller.
Receiver packing and canonical frame support have independent feature flags. Neither creates a counted convention by itself. Receiver packing copies the packed layout, not the observable argument count, so rest slots survive prefixing this.
Canonical counted constructors use the same argument order as ordinary closures; cache comparisons select the active typed pointer member.

Hunk decisions and witnesses

Checked union narrowing is retained instead of incoming unchecked ir.Narrow. Array predicate narrowing retains the declared element contract and checks the runtime array brand.
Witnesses: e4eec87_f2_union_narrow_call.a, e4eec87_f2b_union_narrow_number.a, host_array_predicate.a, host_array_unknown_predicate.a. All passed the Node oracle in both backends.
Break.Depth retains scope and finally cleanup. Break.Label and Continue.Label use their named target and perform the corresponding cleanup.
Witnesses: taste_labels.a and stage3/fixtures/taste/23_labels_finally.a. Both passed the Node oracle.
Nested preallocation does not replace definite-assignment declarations. Non-null assertions unwrap synthetic checked union loads before performing their own nullish check.
Witnesses: non_null.a, non_null_definite.a, non_null_initialized.a; the latter two passed after restoring field readiness on writes.
Imported const labels retain front-3's proof. Host effectful case expressions remain accepted and short-circuited. Literal-only cases retain main's original emission.
Witnesses: imported_const_cases/*, switch_case_declarations/*, taste_stage3_representations.a, and the switch mutants.
New joining witnesses: closure_convention_nested.a and closure_convention_receiver_rest.a; Node agreement, sanitizers, release and leak checks passed.
Hunk-by-hunk resolution audit: /tmp/closure-convention-front-hunk-decisions.json.

Runtime audit

Searches: rg -n -e '->code\s*\(' -e '\.code\s*\(' -e 'counted_code\s*\(' internal/native/runtime, and rg -n adamic_method internal/native/runtime.
Live tree: array.c's sort comparator calls adamic_closure_call(compare, {left,right}, 2). The helper calls adamic_code with two arguments or adamic_counted_code with three. No cast.
adamic.h:137 and :141 are the counted/plain closure invocations; :290 and :291 are the counted/plain method invocations. One typedef per shape.
object.c:67 and :93 retrieve adamic_method_entry; they do not invoke a code pointer. union.c:135 inspects a method table; class_inheritance.c inspects function-index virtual tables.
map_set.c: collection_next ignores presence, so its definition and constructor use adamic_code(self, arguments), with no count.
This branch also carries regexp_replace.c:114 through the typed closure helper. The external library snapshot 132d9919 contains node_process.c:436/:441 and parallel.c:197/:300; those four sites remain outside this branch and their integration is not claimed.

Retains

CLI counted release builds: weak_parent allocations/frees 86/86, retains/releases 253/302, peak 41; typeof_dispatch 9/9, 6/16, peak 3. Both match main.
The previous +2/+2 and +1/+1 were owned Weak/Union values created by fitting fixed call arguments before ownership planning. Fixed fitting remains at the native boundary; only rest-tail elements are fitted in lowering. Counts are numbers and do not retain.
Counts were re-recorded with TestCountsAreRecorded, excluding only stage3/fixtures/taste/21_truthy_loops.a. Its incoming row is preserved, not asserted remeasured.
The complete counts attempt failed because that source casts to a recursive object-field checked view, which interface_cast.go refuses. The source and its expected-success fixture remain intact; the test was not weakened.

Host fixture 24

Exact source preserved as closure-convention-evidence/host24.a, from codex/host-proof-combined. SHA256 4a30cf39a2b30c91703baf39ba4f3574921f30cafedf1c91ee528499c2025159 matches the upstream fixture byte for byte. Node prints false, false, true, false, aBc_09.TS, one per line. At checkpoint 28443efc both C and JS compilation stopped at line 23: stage 0 can't lower node:fs.mkdtempSync yet. The host dependency port below resolves that refusal and establishes end-to-end agreement.
The required filesystem scratch operations are library commit 82c12699, as-const stat options ed957219, with path/process and RegExp callback support on the library branches; they are absent from the three requested compiler tips. Merely changing a closure signature cannot implement those operations. Further library integration must preserve their error and ownership behavior and adapt callback rest slots to this convention.

Runtime audit completeness

The whole merged runtime has exactly four code-pointer invocation sites, all in adamic.h: counted closure at 137, plain closure at 141, counted method at 290 and plain method at 291. Their typedefs are respectively adamic_counted_code, adamic_code, adamic_counted_method and adamic_method. There is no function-pointer cast. The sort caller at array.c:198 dispatches through those closure typedefs.
The requested six source call sites are each listed in closure-convention-evidence/runtime-sites.json. array.c:198 and regexp_replace.c:114 are now present and typed in this branch. The two node_process.c performance sites and two parallel.c sites belong to an external library runtime. Audit is complete; integration of those four sites is incomplete. Their old direct calls must not be accepted as evidence of typed compatibility with this header. Process builtin initializers and callback rest packing also require adaptation, so a five-line call replacement alone would not be a sound port.

Host fixture completion

Observed: exact host fixture 24 is registered as closure_convention_host24.a, with its source unchanged. Both backends agree with Node on false, false, true, false, aBc_09.TS. Release, sanitizers and leak checks passed. Its counted run records allocations/frees 219/219, retains/releases 162/200, peak 53.
The port carries Adamic library scratch operations from 82c12699, exact as-const stat-option proof from ed957219, the lexical join and process directory behavior from codex/host-proof-combined, and guarded RegExp replacement from 96bb40f6 / 132d9919. No cohere code was copied. Unimplemented Node members keep their named refusal.
The callback uses the same counted/plain pointer types and argument order. Its actual count includes captures, offset, input and optional named groups; packing uses the program's reserved rest slot. JS receives the original argument list and uses its existing rest binding. The obsolete library arrow-only rest path was removed, so there is one binding rule.

All agree with Node. The original callback, arguments, throw, argument_guard and group_guard fixtures are preserved, as are scratch mkdtemp and rm fixtures.
Callbacks are accounted for in exception edges, freshness, mutation inference and global move planning. ABI flags are emitted from IR observations, never selected by a name occurring in a user literal. Node host and replacement translation units are omitted when unused; scratch definitions are similarly guarded. The host port leaves the parser C and release binary byte-identical to checkpoint 28443efc: C e5115e8d8daacce460238b6266e9ef3dbe2ecd05aff2fe1c3f47aeb300a95951, binary a0d99447bda0c8d31fb2579d2d7d108221ee11bdf93eed119d13967ededb2c48. Priority ABI enforcement checkpoint

The parser worker found a real silent miscompile in its unpublished scratch
33bf53aca3ce199aa05fe7bd2e7898e7c5ef2d5b. Its evidence at c109c06d records
native 9 versus Node 1, both exit 0 and empty stderr. This is evidence supplied
by that worker; the exact scratch has not yet been rebuilt on this box.

All closure definitions now have a prior declaration using the runtime function
type underlying the one pointer typedef for their shape. Method thunks and
runtime collection_next have the same check. Constructors use C11 _Generic
checks on the unconverted source expression: Clang accepts some function to
void pointer casts even with -pedantic, so an ordinary typed parameter alone
would not forbid that escape. Generic checks reject it without runtime work.
Clang also uses -Wcast-function-type-strict under -Werror.

Every signature-erasing function pointer cast found in the native compiler:
1. class_inheritance.go classDeclarations: (adamic_virtual_method) followed by
   a native method symbol. Removed; the virtual table stores closed-world
   function identities as size_t, never erased function pointers.
2. class_inheritance.go callCode: ((result (*)(parameters))adamic_virtual(...)).
   Removed; an emitted dispatcher switches on that identity and uses typed
   direct calls to the closed-world candidates. C checks each actual signature.
No closure or interface-method pointer cast was present in the reconciled tree.
Object/data pointer casts remain; they do not carry function code.

Pinned mutants in TestClosureConventionWrongOrder, all caught:
- swapped counted definition: conflicting types for adamic_function_4_reader_value;
  previous declaration: static adamic_counted_code_function ...;
- swapped call: incompatible integer to pointer conversion passing int to
  adamic_value *, and incompatible pointer to integer conversion to size_t;
- incompatible function-pointer cast: converts to incompatible function type
  [-Werror,-Wcast-function-type-strict];
- void-pointer-erased constructor: controlling expression type void * not
  compatible with any generic association type.
Full compiler errors: closure-convention-evidence/abi-order-mutants.log.
Generated and runtime drop-count mutants still fail with expected 3, have 2.

Node acceptance includes the exact native-arguments-length-value.a source from
c109c06d, arguments_length_value_count.a, and arguments_length_reduce_left.a.
TestArgumentsLengthTypeScriptSource checks source Node, release -O2 native,
ASan/UBSan native, leak counts, and the JavaScript backend. The uncached final
focused gate passed: native 12.349s before constructor guards; the subsequent
final gate includes those guards and all arguments fixtures (see saved log).
New probe counts: 3 allocations, 3 frees, 2 retains, 7 releases, peak 3.

Post-enforcement validation and legacy slot removal

The IR previously retained ArgumentCountSlot as a misleading name for the end
of fixed/rest storage. It is now FixedArgumentSlots, with no numeric count word
reserved. Rest offsets and emitted C are unchanged; parser C cmp passes against
2b98fb26's output. Legacy code that reads Program.ArgumentCountSlot no longer
builds against this IR. The actual count remains the separate typed parameter.

TestArgumentsLengthWrongSlotMutant replaces the actual binding with
arguments[0].number in the exact parser probe. It compiles, prints 9, exits 0,
and writes no stderr under release and ASan/UBSan. Source Node prints 1.
Both runs are caught only by stdout comparison, reproducing the reported silent
miscompile as a proving mutant; this is not claimed as the exact scratch replay.

Full IR initially found an unapproved direct Call.Function read in non_null.go.
Checked-union synthetic-load recognition now uses CallTargets and requires one
checked helper candidate. It preserves the terminal nullish check and never
peels a multi-target virtual call. The existing closed-world reader guard,
non-null and checked-union fixtures pass; no allowlist exception was added.
Full IR/lower and touched-package go vet then pass (see saved logs).
